- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- Model often overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 65+), overshooting true price by 2–5% in next 5–10 days; apply dampening factor to peak forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows no strong signal (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward lower prices; add 2–4% upward bias to forecast mean.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates downward trends; if true outcome shows 3–5% drop from prior 10-day average, forecast should be adjusted down by 1–3% to match.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, model may still show negative bias — adjust forecast 1–2% upward after 7 days.
